briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 6, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Urgent Climate Crisis: Compound Threats of Heatwaves, Droughts, and Wildfires Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: Today, extreme heatwave advisories have been issued across most parts of the country, with Seoul's daytime high soaring to 39 degrees Celsius and the Yeongdeungpo area reaching 40 degrees Celsius [169]. Southern regions are experiencing an unprecedented compound disaster, with heatwaves, droughts, and algal blooms occurring simultaneously, and an 'attention' level algal bloom alert has been issued for the main stream of the Nakdong River [6, 48, 49, 174]. Such extreme weather is increasing the incidence of heat-related illnesses, and warnings have been issued that in the future, the number of days when people experience 'heat-related illnesses even when doing nothing' could exceed 50 days annually [4, 50, 60, 171, 172]. Internationally, fierce wildfires have erupted across Canada, spreading toxic smoke, and a study has been released indicating that the likelihood of these fires occurring has more than doubled due to human-induced climate change [178, 184, 191, 197, 213, 222]. The UK's National Health Service (NHS) is also experiencing demand pressures akin to winter due to heatwaves caused by the climate crisis, illustrating the intensifying direct impacts of climate change worldwide [223, 224].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response Efforts: Infrastructure Development and Awareness Raising
sections.content: Domestically, there is a growing call for infrastructure development to respond to the climate crisis. Myung Hyun-kwan, Mayor of Haenam County, requested the central government to urgently establish and operate the National Agri-Food Climate Change Response Center to cope with increasingly frequent abnormal weather patterns [2, 5, 11, 25, 36, 39, 41, 59, 91]. In the agricultural sector, Yecheon County is introducing smart irrigation systems, and Jeju Island is promoting the distribution of new varieties of open-field late-harvest citrus adapted to climate change, thus seeking a transition to climate-adaptive agriculture [16, 19, 28, 30, 31, 34, 64]. Furthermore, climate change and carbon neutrality education by corporations and local governments are actively underway: S-OIL has published an ESG report detailing its climate change response achievements [3, 12, 46, 56], AXA General Insurance is providing climate change education for children, and Osan City and Michuhol District are conducting carbon neutrality education and campaigns for businesses and residents, respectively [10, 21, 52, 55, 61, 65, 66, 71, 72, 78, 80, 81, 82, 93, 94, 95, 97]. Korea University is also fostering the next generation of climate leaders by hosting the '2026 Model UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties' [32, 37, 51].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition: Expansion of RE100 and Solar Power by Corporations and Local Governments
sections.content: As the transition to renewable energy accelerates, the groundbreaking ceremony for the 400MW Haenam Solar Power Complex, the largest in Korea, has taken place, targeting completion in 2028 [109, 125, 126, 137, 142, 143, 144, 151, 154, 155, 163, 164, 165, 168]. Corporate efforts towards renewable energy transition are prominent, with HD Hyundai Construction Equipment, for example, expanding the share of renewable energy use at its Incheon plant to over 40% and aiming to achieve RE100 by 2040 [99, 101, 104, 105, 107, 110, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 123, 128, 134, 138, 146, 149, 150, 152, 156, 159, 161, 166]. Furthermore, Representative Park Hee-seung has introduced a special bill concerning the creation of self-sufficient renewable energy cities and support for supply cooperation zones, laying the groundwork for policy support [111, 122, 135, 153]. Solar power is emerging as a national power infrastructure in the AI era [106, 112], and there are also movements to transform industrial complexes into energy production bases by promoting mandatory rooftop solar installations on factories [147].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Climate Crisis Spread and Scientific Warnings
sections.content: The international community is facing the widespread impacts of climate change. Research indicating that human-induced climate change has more than doubled the likelihood of large-scale wildfires in Canada once again emphasizes that climate change is a direct cause of extreme weather events [178, 222]. In Malaysia, durian farmers are reporting crop damage and difficulties due to the effects of climate change [180, 187, 194, 198, 202, 207, 215, 221], and a study has also been released stating that global butterfly habitats are rapidly being reshaped by climate change [7, 181, 211]. Amidst these circumstances, the percentage of people in the United States who acknowledge climate change as a fact shows a decreasing trend [42], suggesting that international consensus and action to address the climate crisis are even more urgently needed [203].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the escalating reality of the global climate crisis and the domestic and international efforts to address it. It is time for our efforts towards a sustainable future to accelerate further. This concludes today's climate briefing.
